playbook.intent: A business analyst picks up a KYC or AML feature in a licensed market, where "we think this is roughly what the rule asks for" will not survive the first supervisory review. It is finished when every requirement points at the clause that forces it, an outside auditor can walk the clause-to-evidence chain without asking the analyst anything, and compliance has signed the exact version being built.
playbook.scope: Domain-specific playbook for a BA on a KYC / AML feature in a regulated FinTech context. Anchors every requirement to a specific regulation clause; produces compliance-grade traceability for audit. Demonstrates how a domain-pack gap would chain end-to-end.

success-criteria.criterion: Every requirement in the onboarding and screening set cites the clause it exists to satisfy by article number, not by a general nod to the directive
A traceability matrix runs clause to requirement to test case to captured evidence, and a reviewer can follow any single row of it end to end unaided
Requirements with no clause behind them are listed apart as business choices, so the compliance officer can see which controls are law and which are house policy
The customer journey is mapped through to the point where a case escalates to manual review, with the trigger threshold and the person who owns the queue both named
A named owner and a review trigger exist for regulatory amendments, so a changed clause arrives as a requirement diff rather than as a supervisory finding
Compliance and engineering have each signed off against a numbered version of the requirement set before any build work starts
